01In Hrušova Lhota we supplied and installed a second-generation BC 4 SBR domestic wastewater treatment plant.

In Hrušova Lhota we supplied and installed a second-generation BC 4 SBR domestic wastewater treatment plant for a family house. The project also included a 5 m³ storage tank fitted with a pump so that the treated water can be used to irrigate the plot by spraying.

The second-generation BC 4 SBR technology installed here uses a modern sequencing batch reactor (SBR) system, notable for its high wastewater treatment efficiency, low running costs and resilience to irregular loads. These qualities make the technology suitable not only for permanently occupied family houses but also for holiday properties, cabins and cottages, where there are long breaks in use. The technology can cope without difficulty with periods of up to 5 months with no wastewater inflow without losing its function.

02Another major advantage of this plant is the declared effluent parameters of the treated water, which meet…

Another major advantage of this plant is the declared effluent parameters of the treated water, which meet the requirements of current legislation and allow the treated water to be discharged safely or reused, for example for irrigation.

What made this project distinctive was the poor hydrogeological conditions and the presence of groundwater. For this reason the tank had to be encased in concrete, which keeps it stable and protects it against being lifted by a high water table.

Once installation was complete, the technology connected and the plant commissioned, the client had a reliable, long-term solution for wastewater treatment, with the option of reusing the treated water on the property.

03Scope of supply: Domestic WWTP BC 4 SBR II.

Scope of supply:

  • Domestic WWTP BC 4 SBR, 2nd generation
  • 5 m³ storage tank
  • Pump for spraying the treated water
  • Concrete encasement of the tanks owing to the presence of groundwater
  • Complete installation, commissioning and operator training

This project confirms that modern wastewater treatment plants can be an effective solution not only for permanently occupied buildings but also for holiday properties with irregular use, where the emphasis is on simple operation, reliability and the long-term stability of the treatment process.
